key_insight: A room-temperature methylammonium polybromide melt can directly convert elemental metal films into bromide perovskites, enabling a universal, single-step, solvent-free synthesis route.
engineering_relevance: This offers a scalable, roll-to-roll-compatible pathway for manufacturing optoelectronic-grade perovskite films from stable metals under ambient conditions.
method: Use methylammonium polybromide melt (PBM) as the reactive bromide source.
React PBM directly with elemental Pb, Sn, Au, and Cu films at room temperature.
Tune PBM composition and leverage metal-mediated comproportionation to control phase evolution, especially for Sn.
evidence_signal: In situ X-ray diffraction tracked phase evolution and captured transient intermediates, while successful formation of MAPbBr3, MASnBr3, MA2Au2Br6, and MA2CuBr4 demonstrated broad reaction scope.
watch_item: Phase selectivity is sensitive to PBM chemistry and redox balance, so overoxidation control is a key implementation risk, especially for Sn.
paper_title: A Universal Polybromide Melt Strategy for the Direct Conversion of Metals into Optoelectronic-Grade Bromide Perovskites
